newsitem.title: USA: Seagram's Bronfman writes song for movie.
newsitem.headline: Seagram's Bronfman writes song for movie.

text.p: Edgar Bronfman Jr., the Canadian billionaire who last year took control of the MCA entertainment giant, is going the extra mile to prove his Hollywood credentials.
Taking time out from his official duties, Bronfman has co-written the theme song for the next Sylvester Stallone action movie, "Daylight," which MCA's Universal Pictures will release Dec. 6.
Under the pseudonym, "Sam Roman," Bronfman worked with longtime collaborator Bruce Roberts on the ballad, "Whenever There Is Love," which Roberts sings with disco diva Donna Summer.

However company officials say Bronfman did not pull any strings to get his song attached to the movie. "I think it's a pleasant coincidence," said Ellen Zoe Golden, spokeswoman for MCA-owed Universal Records, which releases the single on Tuesday.

She said the film's director, Rob Cohen, asked songwriters to submit songs for the movie. Roberts, who has worked with such musicians as Aretha Franklin and Elton John over a two-decade career, sent in "Whenever There Is Love," and it was chosen.
"Then they found out that it was Edgar (as co-writer)," said Golden, adding that it was originally a big secret, "but now we're very proud of it."

"Sam" was the first name of his paternal grandfather who built the family fortune by buying the Seagram Co. Ltd. liquor giant, which owns 80 percent of MCA and of which Edgar Jr. is CEO. "Roman" is the family name of his second wife.
Billboard magazine said the "shuffling power ballad ... swirls with larger-than-life melodrama akin to the kind of summer film it complements."
Radio stations are already playing the single, and the soundtrack album on which it is featured comes out Nov. 19.
